Great idea — an agentic invoice generation system for repair businesses. Let me make sure I understand the core of it:

You want a Next.js web app where users upload 4 Excel files, and an AI agent parses the work descriptions, matches spare parts/tasks from reference data, and generates per-client invoice Excel files — with an iterative review/correction loop before finalizing.

Let me ask the first set of questions to sharpen the requirements:

---

**[1]: What is the invoice template format?**
a. **Excel (.xlsx) template with named cells/ranges** - The agent fills in specific named cells in a pre-existing client template file
b. **Excel template with a fixed structure** - A known row/column layout the agent writes into programmatically
c. **Other** - Describe your template format (e.g., does each client have a unique template file, or one shared template?)

**[2]: How should the AI agent handle ambiguity when parsing the text description?**
a. **Best-guess, flag for review** - Agent picks the most likely spare parts, marks uncertain matches so user can review
b. **Ask before proceeding** - Agent pauses and asks the user to clarify before continuing
c. **Strict match only** - Only include parts it's confident about; leave unmatched items blank for user to fill

**[3]: What is the expected scale per task run?**
a. **Small** - Typically <20 jobs, <5 clients per run
b. **Medium** - 20–100 jobs, 5–20 clients
c. **Large** - 100+ jobs, many clients, needs to handle bulk efficiently

(Answer any subset, e.g. "1=a, 2=b, 3=a" or provide your own answer)

Got it. Updating the plan:
- Invoice templates are Excel files with a fixed known structure
- Agent uses best-guess with flagged comments in the total table for uncertain matches
- Medium scale: 20–100 jobs, 5–20 clients per run

---

**[4]: For the iterative correction loop — how does the user interact with corrections?**
a. **In-app UI** - User edits results directly in the web app (e.g., a table editor), then re-generates
b. **Re-upload corrected file** - User downloads, edits in Excel, re-uploads the corrected version
c. **Natural language chat** - User types corrections like "remove job 5", "move part X to device Y", and the agent applies them

**[5]: Authentication & multi-user — who uses this app?**
a. **Single user / personal tool** - No login needed, one person runs it locally or on a private server
b. **Small team, simple auth** - A few users, basic username/password login is fine
c. **Multi-tenant** - Multiple independent users/companies, each with isolated data and tasks

**[6]: The 4th file links devices to compatible spare parts — how should the agent use this when a part doesn't match the device?**
a. **Hard block** - Reject the part entirely, flag it as incompatible in the output
b. **Soft warning** - Include the part but add a warning comment in the total table
c. **Ignore compatibility** - Trust the text description, don't cross-check device-part compatibility

(Answer any subset, e.g. "4=c, 5=a, 6=b")

Perfect. Updating:
- Corrections: user can re-upload OR type natural language corrections (agent applies them to current state)
- Auth: simple/no auth — this is a POC
- Incompatible parts: soft warning with comment in total table

---

One more round to nail down the technical details:

**[7]: For the Excel invoice template — what does "fixed structure" look like?**
a. **Header block + line items table** - Top section has client info, date, invoice number; below is a table with rows for each work item
b. **Fully custom per client** - Each client template can look different (different cell positions for the same fields)
c. **Single shared template** - One template for all clients, client name/details just get filled in

**[8]: AWS Bedrock — do you have a preferred model in mind?**
a. **Claude (Anthropic)** - Strong at parsing unstructured text, good reasoning
b. **Nova / Titan (Amazon)** - Native AWS models, potentially lower cost
c. **No preference** - Pick whatever works best for the parsing task

**[9]: For the output ZIP — the `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` summary file: how should it be structured?**
a. **One sheet, grouped by client** - All jobs in one sheet, sorted/grouped by client with subtotals
b. **One sheet per client** - Each client gets their own sheet tab in the total file, plus individual client files
c. **Both** - Summary sheet + per-client sheets in the total file, AND separate per-client files

(Answer any subset)

Good — fresh project (just a git repo), no existing code. Research confirms:
- **ExcelJS** is the right choice for reading/writing `.xlsx` (full template manipulation, cell-level control)
- **Postgres-based job queue** (via `graphile/worker` or simple polling) fits perfectly for the self-hosted EC2 Docker setup — no Redis needed
- **AWS Bedrock Converse API** is the cleanest abstraction point for the LLM adapter (same interface works for Nova, Claude, etc.; Ollama can be wrapped to match)

---

Here's the full implementation plan:

---

## Implementation Plan — Agentic Invoice Generator

**Problem Statement:**
A Next.js web app that accepts 4 Excel reference files, uses an AI agent to parse free-text repair job descriptions, matches spare parts/tasks from reference data, and generates per-client invoice Excel files — with an iterative natural-language correction loop before the user finalizes and downloads a ZIP archive.

---

**Requirements:**

- Upload 4 Excel input files per task run (jobs, clients/templates, parts catalog, device-parts mapping)
- AI agent parses free-text job descriptions → matches parts from catalog → cross-checks device compatibility
- Uncertain matches flagged with comments in output; incompatible parts get soft warnings
- Output: ZIP with `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` (single sheet, grouped by client) + per-client invoice files filled into their templates
- Iterative correction: re-upload corrected file OR type natural language corrections
- Task lifecycle: draft → processing → review → completed (archived until manually deleted)
- Stack: Next.js (App Router) + Postgres + Docker on EC2; Bedrock Nova Lite 2 with swappable LLM adapter
- POC: no auth required

---

**Background:**

- **ExcelJS** handles both reading input `.xlsx` and writing into per-client templates with cell-level precision
- **Bedrock Converse API** (`@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`) provides a unified message format; wrapping it in a thin adapter interface makes swapping to Ollama or Vercel AI SDK a one-file change
- **Postgres job queue** (simple `jobs` table with status polling) is sufficient for medium scale on self-hosted EC2 — no Redis needed
- **Next.js App Router** server actions handle file uploads and trigger background processing via a Node.js worker process (separate process or `setImmediate` loop polling the DB)
- Files stored on EBS-mounted volume (via Docker volume), not in DB (only paths stored in DB)

---

**Proposed Solution:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User uploads 4 xlsx files + optional instructions] --> B[Task created in Postgres]
    B --> C[Worker picks up task]
    C --> D[Parse all 4 xlsx files with ExcelJS]
    D --> E[For each job row: send description + parts catalog to LLM adapter]
    E --> F{Confident match?}
    F -- Yes --> G[Add parts to job result]
    F -- No --> H[Add parts with comment flag]
    G & H --> I[Cross-check device-parts compatibility via file 4]
    I --> J[Build total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx grouped by client]
    J --> K[Fill per-client invoice templates]
    K --> L[ZIP all files, store on EBS]
    L --> M[Task status → review]
    M --> N{User satisfied?}
    N -- Natural language correction --> O[LLM applies correction to task state in DB]
    O --> J
    N -- Re-upload file --> P[Replace file, re-run from step D]
    P --> D
    N -- Complete --> Q[Task archived]
```

---

**Task Breakdown:**

**Task 1: Project scaffold & data model**
- Objective: Initialize Next.js app with Postgres connection, define DB schema, set up Docker Compose
- Implementation: `create-next-app`, add `pg`/`drizzle-orm`, define tables: `tasks` (id, status, created_at, instructions), `task_files` (task_id, role enum, file_path), `task_results` (task_id, result_json, zip_path, created_at), `correction_log` (task_id, message, applied_at). Docker Compose: next + postgres containers with EBS volume mount
- Demo: `docker compose up` starts both containers; DB migrations run; `/api/health` returns 200 with DB ping

**Task 2: File upload UI + API**
- Objective: User can create a task, upload 4 xlsx files, add optional instructions, and see the task in a list
- Implementation: Single-page UI with 4 labeled file inputs + textarea for instructions. `POST /api/tasks` creates task record. `POST /api/tasks/[id]/files` saves files to `/data/tasks/<id>/` on EBS volume, records paths in `task_files`. Task list shows id, status, created_at
- Demo: Upload 4 files → task appears in list with status `uploaded`

**Task 3: Excel parsing layer**
- Objective: Parse all 4 input xlsx files into typed in-memory structures
- Implementation: `lib/excel/parser.ts` — functions `parseJobsFile()`, `parseClientsFile()`, `parsePartsFile()`, `parseDevicePartsFile()` using ExcelJS. Each returns a typed array. Write unit tests with sample fixture xlsx files covering normal rows + edge cases (empty description, missing client id)
- Demo: Unit tests pass; parser functions return correct typed objects from fixture files

**Task 4: LLM adapter interface + Bedrock implementation**
- Objective: Thin adapter so the AI call is swappable without touching business logic
- Implementation: `lib/llm/adapter.ts` defines interface `LLMAdapter { complete(prompt: string): Promise<string> }`. `lib/llm/bedrock.ts` implements it using `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` Converse API targeting `amazon.nova-lite-v1`. Adapter selected via `LLM_PROVIDER` env var (`bedrock` | `ollama` | `vercel`). Stub `ollama.ts` implementation for local dev (calls `http://localhost:11434`)
- Demo: Unit test calls the adapter with a sample prompt and gets a string response back (mock in CI, real Bedrock call in integration test)

**Task 5: Agentic parsing — match parts to jobs**
- Objective: For each job row, use the LLM to extract mentioned parts/tasks and match them to the parts catalog
- Implementation: `lib/agent/matchParts.ts` — builds a prompt with the job description + parts catalog (file 3) + device info (file 4). LLM returns structured JSON: `{ matches: [{partId, confidence, note?}] }`. Post-process: confidence < threshold → add `note` as comment flag. Cross-check partId against device-parts map (file 4) → add `compatibilityWarning` if mismatch. Write unit tests with mocked LLM responses
- Demo: Given a fixture job description, `matchParts()` returns correct part matches with flags; incompatible part gets a warning field

**Task 6: Background worker + task processing pipeline**
- Objective: Wire the agent into an async worker that processes tasks end-to-end
- Implementation: `worker/index.ts` — Node.js process that polls `tasks` table for `status = 'queued'` every 5s, claims a task (UPDATE with row lock), runs the full pipeline: parse → match all jobs → build result JSON → store in `task_results`. Update task status through `processing` → `review`. Next.js API route `POST /api/tasks/[id]/process` sets status to `queued` to trigger it
- Demo: Upload files → click "Process" → task status changes to `processing` then `review` within ~30s; result JSON visible in DB

**Task 7: Excel output generation**
- Objective: Generate `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` and per-client invoice files from result JSON
- Implementation: `lib/excel/generator.ts` — `buildTotalSheet(results)` creates grouped-by-client sheet with subtotals and comment cells for flags. `fillClientTemplate(templatePath, clientJobs)` opens client's template xlsx, finds the date cell, line items table start row, and total row (by scanning for known markers), writes data, saves to `/data/tasks/<id>/output/`. `buildZip()` zips all output files. Unit tests for both functions with fixture templates
- Demo: Given fixture result JSON + template files, generator produces a valid ZIP with correct data in the right cells

**Task 8: Review UI — display results & corrections**
- Objective: User can view the processed results, download the ZIP, and submit corrections
- Implementation: Task detail page `/tasks/[id]` — shows status, result table (jobs grouped by client, parts, flags highlighted), download ZIP button. Correction panel: textarea for natural language input + "Apply" button → `POST /api/tasks/[id]/corrections`. Re-upload panel: replace any of the 4 input files → re-triggers processing. Status polling via `setInterval` fetch on the task status endpoint
- Demo: After processing, user sees result table with warnings highlighted; can download ZIP; can type "remove job 3" and see it applied

**Task 9: Natural language correction agent**
- Objective: Apply user's free-text corrections to the task result state
- Implementation: `lib/agent/applyCorrection.ts` — sends current result JSON + correction message to LLM, returns updated result JSON. Supported operations: remove job, add/remove part from job, move part to different device, edit quantity. Saves correction to `correction_log`. Re-runs output generation (Task 7) after applying. Unit tests with mocked LLM for each correction type
- Demo: "Remove job 5" → result JSON updated, new ZIP generated, UI reflects change

**Task 10: Task lifecycle — complete & archive**
- Objective: User can mark a task as completed; completed tasks are listed and preserved
- Implementation: `POST /api/tasks/[id]/complete` sets status to `completed`. Home page shows two sections: active tasks and completed archive. Completed tasks show download link to their ZIP. `DELETE /api/tasks/[id]` removes task record + files from disk (manual deletion only)
- Demo: Complete a task → it moves to archive section; ZIP still downloadable; delete button removes it entirely

---

## Implementation Plan — Agentic Invoice Generator

**Problem Statement:**
A Next.js web app where authenticated users upload 4 Excel reference files per task, and a LangGraph.js agent parses free-text repair job descriptions, matches spare parts from a catalog, and generates per-client invoice Excel files — with an iterative natural-language correction loop before archiving completed tasks.

---

**Requirements:**
- Basic auth (credentials-based, POC level) to block unauthenticated access
- Upload 4 Excel input files per task + optional global/per-row instructions
- LangGraph.js agent: parse jobs → match parts → check device compatibility → generate output
- Uncertain matches flagged with comments; incompatible parts get soft warnings in total sheet
- Output: ZIP with `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` (single sheet, grouped by client) + per-client invoice files
- Per-client templates have hardcoded headers; agent fills date, line items table, total row
- Iterative corrections: re-upload file OR natural language (agent applies to current state)
- Task lifecycle: uploaded → queued → processing → review → completed (archived)
- Stack: Next.js App Router + TypeORM + Postgres + Docker on EC2; LangGraph.js orchestration
- LLM: LiteLLM proxy (OpenAI-compatible) in dev → Bedrock Nova Lite 2 in prod via env config
- OOP style, TypeScript throughout

---

**Background:**
- **LangGraph.js** (`@langchain/langgraph`) models the agent as a `StateGraph` — each processing step (parse, match, validate, generate) is a typed node; edges handle routing and retry loops
- **LLM adapter**: `@langchain/openai` `ChatOpenAI` class with configurable `baseURL` + `apiKey` — points to LiteLLM proxy in dev, Bedrock OpenAI-compatible endpoint in prod; zero code change between environments
- **TypeORM** with a global `DataSource` singleton (cached on `global` in dev to survive HMR); entities imported explicitly
- **next-auth v5** credentials provider: hashed password stored in DB, session stored as JWT cookie — minimal but sufficient for POC
- **ExcelJS** for all xlsx read/write; template filling by scanning for marker rows/cells
- **Background worker**: separate Node.js process (`worker/index.ts`) polling Postgres `tasks` table — avoids Next.js serverless timeout constraints; runs as second process in the same Docker container via `concurrently`

---

**Proposed Solution:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User logs in] --> B[Create task, upload 4 xlsx + instructions]
    B --> C[Task saved to DB, files to EBS]
    C --> D[Click Process → status = queued]
    D --> E[Worker polls DB, picks up task]
    E --> F[LangGraph: ParseNode]
    F --> G[LangGraph: MatchPartsNode - per job]
    G --> H[LangGraph: ValidateCompatibilityNode]
    H --> I[LangGraph: GenerateOutputNode]
    I --> J[ZIP created on EBS, status = review]
    J --> K{User reviews}
    K -- Download ZIP --> L[User checks in Excel]
    K -- Natural language correction --> M[LangGraph: CorrectionNode]
    M --> I
    K -- Re-upload file --> F
    K -- Complete --> N[status = completed, archived]
    N --> O[Manual delete only]
```

---

**Task Breakdown:**

**Task 1: Project scaffold, Docker setup & DB schema**
- Objective: Runnable Next.js + Postgres environment with TypeORM entities and migrations
- Implementation: `create-next-app --typescript`, add `typeorm`, `pg`, `reflect-metadata`. Define entities: `User`, `Task`, `TaskFile` (role enum: jobs/clients/parts/devices), `TaskResult`, `CorrectionLog`. `DataSource` singleton in `lib/db/dataSource.ts` (cached on `global` for HMR safety). Docker Compose: `app` + `postgres` containers, EBS volume mounted at `/data`. Migration script via TypeORM CLI
- Demo: `docker compose up` → app starts, DB migrates, `/api/health` returns 200 with DB connection confirmed

**Task 2: Authentication**
- Objective: Only authenticated users can access the app
- Implementation: `next-auth` v5 with credentials provider. `User` entity stores `username` + `bcrypt`-hashed password. `AuthService` class handles login/verify. Middleware in `middleware.ts` protects all routes except `/login`. Seed script creates one default admin user from env vars. Login page at `/login`
- Demo: Unauthenticated request to `/` redirects to `/login`; valid credentials grant access; invalid credentials show error

**Task 3: Task management UI & API**
- Objective: User can create tasks, upload 4 xlsx files with instructions, and see task list with statuses
- Implementation: `TaskService` class (TypeORM repository). `POST /api/tasks` creates task. `POST /api/tasks/[id]/files` saves files to `/data/tasks/<id>/input/` via `formidable`, records in `TaskFile`. Home page lists tasks with status badges. Task detail page shows uploaded files + instructions fields (global + per-file). `PATCH /api/tasks/[id]` saves instructions
- Demo: Create task → upload 4 files → add instructions → task appears in list with status `uploaded`

**Task 4: Excel parsing layer (OOP)**
- Objective: Parse all 4 input xlsx files into typed domain objects
- Implementation: Abstract base class `ExcelParser<T>`, concrete classes: `JobsParser`, `ClientsParser`, `PartsParser`, `DevicePartsParser` — each implements `parse(filePath: string): Promise<T[]>` using ExcelJS. Typed interfaces: `JobRow`, `ClientRow`, `PartRow`, `DevicePartRow`. Unit tests with fixture xlsx files covering normal rows + edge cases (empty description, missing fields)
- Demo: Unit tests pass; each parser returns correctly typed arrays from fixture files

**Task 5: LLM adapter (LiteLLM dev / Bedrock prod)**
- Objective: Single LLM interface usable in both dev and prod without code changes
- Implementation: Abstract class `LLMAdapter` with `complete(systemPrompt: string, userPrompt: string): Promise<string>`. Concrete `OpenAICompatibleAdapter` uses `@langchain/openai` `ChatOpenAI` with `baseURL` + `apiKey` from env (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_MODEL`). In dev: points to LiteLLM proxy. In prod: points to Bedrock OpenAI-compatible endpoint. `LLMAdapterFactory.create()` reads env and returns correct instance. Unit test with mocked HTTP
- Demo: `LLMAdapterFactory.create()` returns correct adapter per env; mock test confirms prompt/response round-trip

**Task 6: LangGraph agent — core invoice pipeline**
- Objective: LangGraph `StateGraph` that processes a task end-to-end: parse → match parts → validate → generate output
- Implementation: `InvoiceAgentState` typed schema. Four nodes as classes implementing `invoke(state)`:
  - `ParseNode`: runs all 4 parsers, stores results in state
  - `MatchPartsNode`: for each job, calls LLM with description + parts catalog → returns `{partId, confidence, note?}[]`; low-confidence items flagged
  - `ValidateCompatibilityNode`: cross-checks matched parts against device-parts map; adds `compatibilityWarning` where needed
  - `GenerateOutputNode`: builds total xlsx + fills client templates + zips output
  - Edges: linear flow with conditional retry edge from `GenerateOutputNode` back to `MatchPartsNode` if correction requested
- Demo: Given fixture input files, running the graph produces a valid ZIP with correct total sheet and per-client files

**Task 7: Excel output generation (OOP)**
- Objective: Generate `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` and fill per-client invoice templates
- Implementation: `TotalSheetBuilder` class: builds single sheet grouped by client, subtotals, comment cells for flags/warnings. `ClientTemplateWriter` class: opens template xlsx, locates date cell + line items table start + total row by scanning for known structural markers, writes data. `OutputZipper` class: assembles ZIP from all output files. Unit tests with fixture templates
- Demo: Unit tests confirm correct cell values in generated files; warnings appear as Excel cell comments

**Task 8: Background worker wiring**
- Objective: Worker process picks up queued tasks and runs the LangGraph agent
- Implementation: `worker/index.ts` — `WorkerService` class polls `tasks` WHERE `status = 'queued'` every 5s with `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Claims task, instantiates `InvoiceAgent` (the compiled LangGraph), invokes it, updates status to `processing` → `review` on success or `failed` on error with error message stored. Run alongside Next.js via `concurrently` in `package.json` dev/start scripts. `POST /api/tasks/[id]/process` sets status to `queued`
- Demo: Upload files → click "Process" → status cycles to `review` within ~30s; ZIP path stored in DB

**Task 9: Review UI — results display, download & corrections**
- Objective: User reviews results, downloads ZIP, and submits natural language corrections
- Implementation: Task detail page (status=`review`): result summary table showing jobs grouped by client, flagged items highlighted in yellow, warnings in orange. Download ZIP button. Correction panel: textarea + "Apply Correction" button → `POST /api/tasks/[id]/corrections` → saves to `CorrectionLog`, re-queues task. Re-upload panel: replace any input file → re-queues task. Status auto-refreshes every 3s via polling
- Demo: Processed task shows result table with flags; "remove job 3" correction re-triggers processing and updates output

**Task 10: Correction node in LangGraph**
- Objective: Apply natural language corrections to task state before re-generating output
- Implementation: `CorrectionNode` added to the graph — activated when `state.pendingCorrection` is set. Sends current result JSON + correction message to LLM → returns updated result JSON. Supported operations: remove job, add/remove/move part, edit quantity. After applying, graph continues to `GenerateOutputNode`. Unit tests with mocked LLM for each correction type
- Demo: "Move the toner cartridge from job 2 to job 4" → result JSON updated correctly → new ZIP generated

**Task 11: Task lifecycle completion & archive**
- Objective: User completes a task; completed tasks are archived and browsable
- Implementation: `POST /api/tasks/[id]/complete` sets status to `completed`. Home page: two sections — "Active Tasks" and "Completed Archive". Completed tasks show date, client count, download ZIP link. `DELETE /api/tasks/[id]` (admin only): removes DB record + deletes files from EBS. Completed tasks are read-only (no corrections)
- Demo: Complete a task → moves to archive; ZIP still downloadable; delete removes it from list and disk

Good question to settle before we start building. Here's my thinking:

---

**UI Component Library**

For a data-heavy internal tool (tables, file uploads, status badges, modals) on desktop only, the realistic options are:

- **shadcn/ui** — not a library you install, it's copy-paste components built on Radix UI primitives + Tailwind. You own the code, no version lock-in, excellent TypeScript support, very popular in Next.js App Router projects. Best fit for a POC that might grow.
- **Ant Design** — full component library, has a powerful `Table` component with grouping/sorting built in (useful for your results view), but it's heavy, opinionated, and has its own CSS-in-JS that can conflict with Next.js SSR.
- **Mantine** — full library, good table/form components, works well with Next.js, lighter than Ant Design.

My recommendation: **shadcn/ui**. It gives you exactly what you need (Table, Dialog, Badge, Form, Tabs) without fighting the framework, and Tailwind handles all layout/spacing. For the results table with grouping you'd use **TanStack Table v8** underneath (shadcn's DataTable pattern already uses it).

---

**Styling**

**Tailwind CSS v4** — pairs naturally with shadcn/ui, desktop-only means no complex responsive breakpoint logic needed, utility classes keep styles co-located with components. No separate CSS files to maintain.

---

**State Management**

For this app, honestly: **probably not needed** as a separate library. Here's why:

- Task list, task detail, correction history → all server state fetched from your API
- **TanStack Query (React Query)** handles server state perfectly: caching, polling (for task status updates every 3s), invalidation after mutations. This replaces what you'd otherwise reach for Redux/Zustand for
- The only local UI state (open/close modal, which tab is active) is simple enough for `useState`

So: **TanStack Query for server state + `useState` for local UI state**. No Zustand/Redux needed for a POC of this scope.

---

**Summary proposal:**

| Concern | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Components | shadcn/ui + Radix UI | Owns the code, Next.js native, great DX |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 | Co-located, desktop-only = simple |
| Data tables | TanStack Table v8 | Grouping, sorting, shadcn DataTable pattern |
| Server state | TanStack Query v5 | Polling, caching, mutations |
| Local UI state | `useState` | Nothing complex enough to warrant more |

REST is the right call here, and I agree with your instinct. Here's the quick reasoning:

**Why not GraphQL or gRPC:**
- GraphQL adds a schema layer, resolver boilerplate, and a client (Apollo/urql) — overkill when your data shapes are straightforward and you have maybe 10 endpoints
- gRPC is for service-to-service communication, not browser clients — wrong tool entirely here
- Both add complexity that works against the POC goal

**REST fits perfectly because:**
- Next.js App Router Route Handlers are REST-native
- TanStack Query works best with simple `fetch` calls to REST endpoints
- Your operations are resource-oriented: tasks, files, corrections, results — maps cleanly to REST nouns
- File uploads (multipart/form-data) are trivial with REST, awkward with GraphQL

**One nuance worth noting:** since you're using Next.js App Router, some of these "API calls" could be **Server Actions** instead of REST endpoints — particularly mutations like "mark complete" or "apply correction". Server Actions are essentially typed RPC calls co-located with your components, no fetch boilerplate needed. But for anything TanStack Query needs to poll or cache (task status, results), a proper REST route handler is cleaner.

**Proposed split:**
- REST route handlers (`/api/...`) — file uploads, task status polling, ZIP download
- Server Actions — simple mutations (complete task, delete task, save instructions)

## Implementation Plan — Agentic Invoice Generator

**Problem Statement:**
A Next.js web app where authenticated users upload 4 Excel reference files per task, and a LangGraph.js agent parses free-text repair job descriptions, matches spare parts from a catalog, and generates per-client invoice Excel files — with an iterative natural-language correction loop before archiving completed tasks.

---

**Requirements:**
- Basic auth (credentials-based, POC level) to block unauthenticated access
- Upload 4 Excel input files per task + optional global/per-row instructions
- LangGraph.js agent: parse jobs → match parts → check device compatibility → generate output
- Uncertain matches flagged with comments; incompatible parts get soft warnings in total sheet
- Output: ZIP with `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` (single sheet, grouped by client) + per-client invoice files
- Per-client templates have hardcoded headers; agent fills date, line items table, total row
- Iterative corrections: re-upload file OR natural language (agent applies to current state)
- Task lifecycle: uploaded → queued → processing → review → completed (archived)
- Stack: Next.js App Router + TypeORM + Postgres + Docker on EC2; LangGraph.js orchestration
- LLM: LiteLLM proxy (OpenAI-compatible) in dev → Bedrock Nova Lite 2 in prod via env config
- UI: shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS v4 + TanStack Table v8; desktop (FHD) only
- State: TanStack Query v5 for server state, `useState` for local UI state
- API: REST route handlers for uploads/polling/downloads; Server Actions for simple mutations
- No NestJS — plain TypeScript service classes with manual DI via `container.ts` singleton registry
- OOP style, TypeScript throughout

---

**Background:**
- **LangGraph.js** (`@langchain/langgraph`) — `StateGraph` with typed state schema; each processing step is a typed node class
- **LLM adapter**: `ChatOpenAI` from `@langchain/openai` with configurable `baseURL`+`apiKey` — LiteLLM proxy in dev, Bedrock OpenAI-compatible endpoint in prod; zero code change between environments
- **TypeORM** global `DataSource` singleton cached on `global` for HMR safety; entities imported explicitly
- **next-auth v5** credentials provider: bcrypt-hashed password in DB, JWT session cookie
- **ExcelJS** for all xlsx read/write; template filling by scanning for structural markers
- **Background worker**: standalone Node.js process polling Postgres with `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; runs alongside Next.js via `concurrently`
- **Manual DI**: `lib/container.ts` instantiates all service singletons at startup (`TaskService`, `AuthService`, `LLMAdapterFactory`, etc.) and exports them — no framework needed
- **shadcn/ui DataTable** pattern uses TanStack Table v8 — handles grouping/sorting for results view

---

**Proposed Solution:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User logs in] --> B[Create task, upload 4 xlsx + instructions]
    B --> C[Task saved to DB, files to EBS]
    C --> D[Click Process → status = queued]
    D --> E[Worker polls DB, picks up task]
    E --> F[LangGraph: ParseNode]
    F --> G[LangGraph: MatchPartsNode - per job]
    G --> H[LangGraph: ValidateCompatibilityNode]
    H --> I[LangGraph: GenerateOutputNode]
    I --> J[ZIP created on EBS, status = review]
    J --> K{User reviews}
    K -- Download ZIP --> L[User checks in Excel]
    K -- Natural language correction --> M[LangGraph: CorrectionNode]
    M --> I
    K -- Re-upload file --> F
    K -- Complete --> N[status = completed, archived]
```

**Task 1: Project scaffold, Docker setup, DB schema & DI container**
- Objective: Runnable Next.js + Postgres environment with TypeORM entities, migrations, and service container
- Implementation: `create-next-app --typescript`, add `typeorm`, `pg`, `reflect-metadata`, `tailwindcss`, `shadcn/ui` init. Entities: `User`, `Task`, `TaskFile` (role enum: jobs/clients/parts/devices), `TaskResult`, `CorrectionLog`. `DataSource` singleton in `lib/db/dataSource.ts` cached on `global`. `lib/container.ts` instantiates and exports all service singletons. Docker Compose: `app` + `postgres`, EBS volume at `/data`. TypeORM CLI migration script.
- Demo: `docker compose up` → app starts, DB migrates, `/api/health` returns 200 with DB ping

**Task 2: Authentication**
- Objective: Only authenticated users can access the app
- Implementation: `next-auth` v5 credentials provider. `AuthService` class in container: `verifyCredentials(username, password)` with bcrypt. Middleware protects all routes except `/login`. Seed script creates default admin from env vars (`ADMIN_USER`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`). Login page with shadcn `Card` + `Form`.
- Demo: Unauthenticated `/` redirects to `/login`; valid credentials grant access; invalid shows error

**Task 3: Task management UI & API**
- Objective: User can create tasks, upload 4 xlsx files with instructions, and see task list
- Implementation: `TaskService` class (TypeORM repository, registered in container). REST: `POST /api/tasks`, `POST /api/tasks/[id]/files` (multipart, saves to `/data/tasks/<id>/input/`). - Objective: `StateGraph` processing a task end-to-end: parse → match → validate → generate
- Implementation: `InvoiceAgentState` typed schema. Node classes: `ParseNode`, `MatchPartsNode` (LLM call per job → `{partId, confidence, note?}[]`, flags low-confidence), `ValidateCompatibilityNode` (cross-checks device-parts map, adds `compatibilityWarning`), `GenerateOutputNode` (delegates to Task 7 classes). - Demo: Running the graph on fixture inputs produces a valid ZIP with correct total sheet and per-client files

**Task 7: Excel output generation (OOP)**
- Objective: Generate `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` and fill per-client invoice templates
- Implementation: `TotalSheetBuilder`: single sheet grouped by client, subtotals, Excel cell comments for flags/warnings. `ClientTemplateWriter`: opens template, locates date cell + line items table + total row by structural scanning, writes data. `OutputZipper`: assembles final ZIP. All registered in container. Unit tests with fixture templates.
- Demo: Unit tests confirm correct cell values; warnings appear as Excel cell comments

**Task 8: Background worker wiring**
- Objective: Worker process picks up queued tasks and runs the LangGraph agent
- Implementation: `WorkerService` class in `worker/index.ts` — uses container to get `InvoiceAgent` + `TaskService`; polls `tasks WHERE status='queued'` every 5s with `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; updates status `processing` → `review` or `failed` with error stored. Run via `concurrently` in npm scripts. REST: `POST /api/tasks/[id]/process` sets status to `queued`.
- Demo: Upload files → click "Process" → status cycles to `review` within ~30s

**Task 9: Review UI — results display, download & corrections**
- Objective: User reviews results, downloads ZIP, submits corrections
- Implementation: Task detail page (status=`review`): TanStack Table grouped by client, flagged rows highlighted (yellow = uncertain, orange = compatibility warning). REST: `GET /api/tasks/[id]/download` streams ZIP. Correction panel: shadcn `Textarea` + button → `POST /api/tasks/[id]/corrections` → saves to `CorrectionLog`, re-queues task. Re-upload panel replaces input file + re-queues. TanStack Query polls `GET /api/tasks/[id]` every 3s while `processing`.
- Demo: Result table shows flags; correction re-triggers processing; status updates live in UI

**Task 10: Correction node in LangGraph**
- Objective: Apply natural language corrections to task state before re-generating output
- Implementation: `CorrectionNode` activated when `state.pendingCorrection` is set — sends result JSON + correction message to LLM → returns updated result JSON. Supported: remove job, add/remove/move part, edit quantity. Graph continues to `GenerateOutputNode` after applying. Unit tests with mocked LLM per correction type.
- Demo: "Move toner cartridge from job 2 to job 4" → result JSON updated → new ZIP generated

**Task 11: Task lifecycle completion & archive**
- Objective: Completed tasks archived, browsable, manually deletable
- Implementation: Server Action `completeTask(taskId)` sets status `completed`. Home page: two shadcn `Tabs` — "Active" and "Archive". Completed tasks: read-only, show date/client count/download link. Server Action `deleteTask(taskId)`: removes DB record + EBS files.
- Demo: Complete task → moves to Archive tab; ZIP downloadable; delete removes from list and disk

- Components: shadcn/ui + Radix UI primitives
- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4
- Data tables: TanStack Table v8 (via shadcn DataTable pattern)
- Server state: TanStack Query v5

1=b; 2=a (if doubts, leaves comment in the rsult total table); 3=b

Got it. Updating the plan:
- Invoice templates are Excel files with a fixed known structure
- Agent uses best-guess with flagged comments in the total table for uncertain matches
- Medium scale: 20–100 jobs, 5–20 clients per run

---

**[4]: For the iterative correction loop — how does the user interact with corrections?**
a. **In-app UI** - User edits results directly in the web app (e.g., a table editor), then re-generates
b. **Re-upload corrected file** - User downloads, edits in Excel, re-uploads the corrected version
c. **Natural language chat** - User types corrections like "remove job 5", "move part X to device Y", and the agent applies them

**[5]: Authentication & multi-user — who uses this app?**
a. **Single user / personal tool** - No login needed, one person runs it locally or on a private server
b. **Small team, simple auth** - A few users, basic username/password login is fine
c. **Multi-tenant** - Multiple independent users/companies, each with isolated data and tasks

**[6]: The 4th file links devices to compatible spare parts — how should the agent use this when a part doesn't match the device?**
a. **Hard block** - Reject the part entirely, flag it as incompatible in the output
b. **Soft warning** - Include the part but add a warning comment in the total table
c. **Ignore compatibility** - Trust the text description, don't cross-check device-part compatibility

(Answer any subset, e.g. "4=c, 5=a, 6=b")
4=b,c(can re-upload file, but can add natural language corrections for current uploaded files); 5=(keep it simple, it is POC); 6=b

Perfect. Updating:
- Corrections: user can re-upload OR type natural language corrections (agent applies them to current state)
- Auth: simple/no auth — this is a POC
- Incompatible parts: soft warning with comment in total table

---

One more round to nail down the technical details:

**[7]: For the Excel invoice template — what does "fixed structure" look like?**
a. **Header block + line items table** - Top section has client info, date, invoice number; below is a table with rows for each work item
b. **Fully custom per client** - Each client template can look different (different cell positions for the same fields)
c. **Single shared template** - One template for all clients, client name/details just get filled in

**[8]: AWS Bedrock — do you have a preferred model in mind?**
a. **Claude (Anthropic)** - Strong at parsing unstructured text, good reasoning
b. **Nova / Titan (Amazon)** - Native AWS models, potentially lower cost
c. **No preference** - Pick whatever works best for the parsing task

**[9]: For the output ZIP — the `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` summary file: how should it be structured?**
a. **One sheet, grouped by client** - All jobs in one sheet, sorted/grouped by client with subtotals
b. **One sheet per client** - Each client gets their own sheet tab in the total file, plus individual client files
c. **Both** - Summary sheet + per-client sheets in the total file, AND separate per-client files

(Answer any subset)

7=b(but your point of concern is date, table with jobs and total line, all header is hardcoded in the each template); 8=Nova-2-lite for now. (but the app have to be able to switch to local ollama or vercel without heavy refactoring, maybe kinda adapter should be used); 9=a

- Templates are per-client, hardcoded headers; agent fills: date, line items table, total line
- AI: Amazon Nova Lite 2 via Bedrock, but with an LLM adapter pattern so switching to Ollama/Vercel AI is a config change
- Total summary: single sheet, grouped by client with subtotals

content.data:
Good — fresh project (just a git repo), no existing code. Research confirms:
- **ExcelJS** is the right choice for reading/writing `.xlsx` (full template manipulation, cell-level control)
- **Postgres-based job queue** (via `graphile/worker` or simple polling) fits perfectly for the self-hosted EC2 Docker setup — no Redis needed
- **AWS Bedrock Converse API** is the cleanest abstraction point for the LLM adapter (same interface works for Nova, Claude, etc.; Ollama can be wrapped to match)

---

Here's the full implementation plan:

---

## Implementation Plan — Agentic Invoice Generator

**Problem Statement:**
A Next.js web app that accepts 4 Excel reference files, uses an AI agent to parse free-text repair job descriptions, matches spare parts/tasks from reference data, and generates per-client invoice Excel files — with an iterative natural-language correction loop before the user finalizes and downloads a ZIP archive.

---

**Requirements:**

- Upload 4 Excel input files per task run (jobs, clients/templates, parts catalog, device-parts mapping)
- AI agent parses free-text job descriptions → matches parts from catalog → cross-checks device compatibility
- Uncertain matches flagged with comments in output; incompatible parts get soft warnings
- Output: ZIP with `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` (single sheet, grouped by client) + per-client invoice files filled into their templates
- Iterative correction: re-upload corrected file OR type natural language corrections
- Task lifecycle: draft → processing → review → completed (archived until manually deleted)
- Stack: Next.js (App Router) + Postgres + Docker on EC2; Bedrock Nova Lite 2 with swappable LLM adapter
- POC: no auth required

---

**Background:**

- **ExcelJS** handles both reading input `.xlsx` and writing into per-client templates with cell-level precision
- **Bedrock Converse API** (`@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime`) provides a unified message format; wrapping it in a thin adapter interface makes swapping to Ollama or Vercel AI SDK a one-file change
- **Postgres job queue** (simple `jobs` table with status polling) is sufficient for medium scale on self-hosted EC2 — no Redis needed
- **Next.js App Router** server actions handle file uploads and trigger background processing via a Node.js worker process (separate process or `setImmediate` loop polling the DB)
- Files stored on EBS-mounted volume (via Docker volume), not in DB (only paths stored in DB)

---

**Proposed Solution:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User uploads 4 xlsx files + optional instructions] --> B[Task created in Postgres]
    B --> C[Worker picks up task]
    C --> D[Parse all 4 xlsx files with ExcelJS]
    D --> E[For each job row: send description + parts catalog to LLM adapter]
    E --> F{Confident match?}
    F -- Yes --> G[Add parts to job result]
    F -- No --> H[Add parts with comment flag]
    G & H --> I[Cross-check device-parts compatibility via file 4]
    I --> J[Build total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx grouped by client]
    J --> K[Fill per-client invoice templates]
    K --> L[ZIP all files, store on EBS]
    L --> M[Task status → review]
    M --> N{User satisfied?}
    N -- Natural language correction --> O[LLM applies correction to task state in DB]
    O --> J
    N -- Re-upload file --> P[Replace file, re-run from step D]
    P --> D
    N -- Complete --> Q[Task archived]
```

---

**Task Breakdown:**

**Task 1: Project scaffold & data model**
- Objective: Initialize Next.js app with Postgres connection, define DB schema, set up Docker Compose
- Implementation: `create-next-app`, add `pg`/`drizzle-orm`, define tables: `tasks` (id, status, created_at, instructions), `task_files` (task_id, role enum, file_path), `task_results` (task_id, result_json, zip_path, created_at), `correction_log` (task_id, message, applied_at). Docker Compose: next + postgres containers with EBS volume mount
- Demo: `docker compose up` starts both containers; DB migrations run; `/api/health` returns 200 with DB ping

**Task 2: File upload UI + API**
- Objective: User can create a task, upload 4 xlsx files, add optional instructions, and see the task in a list
- Implementation: Single-page UI with 4 labeled file inputs + textarea for instructions. `POST /api/tasks` creates task record. `POST /api/tasks/[id]/files` saves files to `/data/tasks/<id>/` on EBS volume, records paths in `task_files`. Task list shows id, status, created_at
- Demo: Upload 4 files → task appears in list with status `uploaded`

**Task 3: Excel parsing layer**
- Objective: Parse all 4 input xlsx files into typed in-memory structures
- Implementation: `lib/excel/parser.ts` — functions `parseJobsFile()`, `parseClientsFile()`, `parsePartsFile()`, `parseDevicePartsFile()` using ExcelJS. Each returns a typed array. Write unit tests with sample fixture xlsx files covering normal rows + edge cases (empty description, missing client id)
- Demo: Unit tests pass; parser functions return correct typed objects from fixture files

**Task 4: LLM adapter interface + Bedrock implementation**
- Objective: Thin adapter so the AI call is swappable without touching business logic
- Implementation: `lib/llm/adapter.ts` defines interface `LLMAdapter { complete(prompt: string): Promise<string> }`. `lib/llm/bedrock.ts` implements it using `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` Converse API targeting `amazon.nova-lite-v1`. Adapter selected via `LLM_PROVIDER` env var (`bedrock` | `ollama` | `vercel`). Stub `ollama.ts` implementation for local dev (calls `http://localhost:11434`)
- Demo: Unit test calls the adapter with a sample prompt and gets a string response back (mock in CI, real Bedrock call in integration test)

**Task 5: Agentic parsing — match parts to jobs**
- Objective: For each job row, use the LLM to extract mentioned parts/tasks and match them to the parts catalog
- Implementation: `lib/agent/matchParts.ts` — builds a prompt with the job description + parts catalog (file 3) + device info (file 4). LLM returns structured JSON: `{ matches: [{partId, confidence, note?}] }`. Post-process: confidence < threshold → add `note` as comment flag. Cross-check partId against device-parts map (file 4) → add `compatibilityWarning` if mismatch. Write unit tests with mocked LLM responses
- Demo: Given a fixture job description, `matchParts()` returns correct part matches with flags; incompatible part gets a warning field

**Task 6: Background worker + task processing pipeline**

Here's the updated full plan:

---

## Implementation Plan — Agentic Invoice Generator

**Problem Statement:**
A Next.js web app where authenticated users upload 4 Excel reference files per task, and a LangGraph.js agent parses free-text repair job descriptions, matches spare parts from a catalog, and generates per-client invoice Excel files — with an iterative natural-language correction loop before archiving completed tasks.

---

**Requirements:**
- Basic auth (credentials-based, POC level) to block unauthenticated access
- Upload 4 Excel input files per task + optional global/per-row instructions
- LangGraph.js agent: parse jobs → match parts → check device compatibility → generate output
- Uncertain matches flagged with comments; incompatible parts get soft warnings in total sheet
- Output: ZIP with `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` (single sheet, grouped by client) + per-client invoice files
- Per-client templates have hardcoded headers; agent fills date, line items table, total row
- Iterative corrections: re-upload file OR natural language (agent applies to current state)
- Task lifecycle: uploaded → queued → processing → review → completed (archived)
- Stack: Next.js App Router + TypeORM + Postgres + Docker on EC2; LangGraph.js orchestration
- LLM: LiteLLM proxy (OpenAI-compatible) in dev → Bedrock Nova Lite 2 in prod via env config
- OOP style, TypeScript throughout

---

**Background:**
- **LangGraph.js** (`@langchain/langgraph`) models the agent as a `StateGraph` — each processing step (parse, match, validate, generate) is a typed node; edges handle routing and retry loops
- **LLM adapter**: `@langchain/openai` `ChatOpenAI` class with configurable `baseURL` + `apiKey` — points to LiteLLM proxy in dev, Bedrock OpenAI-compatible endpoint in prod; zero code change between environments
- **TypeORM** with a global `DataSource` singleton (cached on `global` in dev to survive HMR); entities imported explicitly
- **next-auth v5** credentials provider: hashed password stored in DB, session stored as JWT cookie — minimal but sufficient for POC
- **ExcelJS** for all xlsx read/write; template filling by scanning for marker rows/cells
- **Background worker**: separate Node.js process (`worker/index.ts`) polling Postgres `tasks` table — avoids Next.js serverless timeout constraints; runs as second process in the same Docker container via `concurrently`

---

**Proposed Solution:**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User logs in] --> B[Create task, upload 4 xlsx + instructions]
    B --> C[Task saved to DB, files to EBS]
    C --> D[Click Process → status = queued]
    D --> E[Worker polls DB, picks up task]
    E --> F[LangGraph: ParseNode]
    F --> G[LangGraph: MatchPartsNode - per job]
    G --> H[LangGraph: ValidateCompatibilityNode]
    H --> I[LangGraph: GenerateOutputNode]
    I --> J[ZIP created on EBS, status = review]
    J --> K{User reviews}
    K -- Download ZIP --> L[User checks in Excel]
    K -- Natural language correction --> M[LangGraph: CorrectionNode]
    M --> I
    K -- Re-upload file --> F
    K -- Complete --> N[status = completed, archived]
    N --> O[Manual delete only]
```

---

**Task Breakdown:**

**Task 1: Project scaffold, Docker setup & DB schema**
- Objective: Runnable Next.js + Postgres environment with TypeORM entities and migrations
- Implementation: `create-next-app --typescript`, add `typeorm`, `pg`, `reflect-metadata`. Define entities: `User`, `Task`, `TaskFile` (role enum: jobs/clients/parts/devices), `TaskResult`, `CorrectionLog`. `DataSource` singleton in `lib/db/dataSource.ts` (cached on `global` for HMR safety). Docker Compose: `app` + `postgres` containers, EBS volume mounted at `/data`. Migration script via TypeORM CLI
- Demo: `docker compose up` → app starts, DB migrates, `/api/health` returns 200 with DB connection confirmed

**Task 2: Authentication**
- Objective: Only authenticated users can access the app
- Implementation: `next-auth` v5 with credentials provider. `User` entity stores `username` + `bcrypt`-hashed password. `AuthService` class handles login/verify. Middleware in `middleware.ts` protects all routes except `/login`. Seed script creates one default admin user from env vars. Login page at `/login`
- Demo: Unauthenticated request to `/` redirects to `/login`; valid credentials grant access; invalid credentials show error

**Task 3: Task management UI & API**
- Objective: User can create tasks, upload 4 xlsx files with instructions, and see task list with statuses
- Implementation: `TaskService` class (TypeORM repository). `POST /api/tasks` creates task. `POST /api/tasks/[id]/files` saves files to `/data/tasks/<id>/input/` via `formidable`, records in `TaskFile`. Home page lists tasks with status badges. Task detail page shows uploaded files + instructions fields (global + per-file). `PATCH /api/tasks/[id]` saves instructions
- Demo: Create task → upload 4 files → add instructions → task appears in list with status `uploaded`

**Task 4: Excel parsing layer (OOP)**
- Objective: Parse all 4 input xlsx files into typed domain objects
- Implementation: Abstract base class `ExcelParser<T>`, concrete classes: `JobsParser`, `ClientsParser`, `PartsParser`, `DevicePartsParser` — each implements `parse(filePath: string): Promise<T[]>` using ExcelJS. Typed interfaces: `JobRow`, `ClientRow`, `PartRow`, `DevicePartRow`. Unit tests with fixture xlsx files covering normal rows + edge cases (empty description, missing fields)
- Demo: Unit tests pass; each parser returns correctly typed arrays from fixture files

**Task 5: LLM adapter (LiteLLM dev / Bedrock prod)**
- Objective: Single LLM interface usable in both dev and prod without code changes
- Implementation: Abstract class `LLMAdapter` with `complete(systemPrompt: string, userPrompt: string): Promise<string>`. Concrete `OpenAICompatibleAdapter` uses `@langchain/openai` `ChatOpenAI` with `baseURL` + `apiKey` from env (`LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_MODEL`). In dev: points to LiteLLM proxy. In prod: points to Bedrock OpenAI-compatible endpoint. `LLMAdapterFactory.create()` reads env and returns correct instance. Unit test with mocked HTTP
- Demo: `LLMAdapterFactory.create()` returns correct adapter per env; mock test confirms prompt/response round-trip

**Task 6: LangGraph agent — core invoice pipeline**
- Objective: LangGraph `StateGraph` that processes a task end-to-end: parse → match parts → validate → generate output
- Implementation: `InvoiceAgentState` typed schema. Four nodes as classes implementing `invoke(state)`:
  - `ParseNode`: runs all 4 parsers, stores results in state
  - `MatchPartsNode`: for each job, calls LLM with description + parts catalog → returns `{partId, confidence, note?}[]`; low-confidence items flagged
  - `ValidateCompatibilityNode`: cross-checks matched parts against device-parts map; adds `compatibilityWarning` where needed
  - `GenerateOutputNode`: builds total xlsx + fills client templates + zips output
  - Edges: linear flow with conditional retry edge from `GenerateOutputNode` back to `MatchPartsNode` if correction requested
- Demo: Given fixture input files, running the graph produces a valid ZIP with correct total sheet and per-client files

**Task 7: Excel output generation (OOP)**
- Objective: Generate `total_YYYY_MM_DD.xlsx` and fill per-client invoice templates
- Implementation: `TotalSheetBuilder` class: builds single sheet grouped by client, subtotals, comment cells for flags/warnings. `ClientTemplateWriter` class: opens template xlsx, locates date cell + line items table start + total row by scanning for known structural markers, writes data. `OutputZipper` class: assembles ZIP from all output files. Unit tests with fixture templates
- Demo: Unit tests confirm correct cell values in generated files; warnings appear as Excel cell comments

**Task 8: Background worker wiring**
- Objective: Worker process picks up queued tasks and runs the LangGraph agent
- Implementation: `worker/index.ts` — `WorkerService` class polls `tasks` WHERE `status = 'queued'` every 5s with `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. Claims task, instantiates `InvoiceAgent` (the compiled LangGraph), invokes it, updates status to `processing` → `review` on success or `failed` on error with error message stored. Run alongside Next.js via `concurrently` in `package.json` dev/start scripts. `POST /api/tasks/[id]/process` sets status to `queued`
- Demo: Upload files → click "Process" → status cycles to `review` within ~30s; ZIP path stored in DB

**Task 9: Review UI — results display, download & corrections**
- Objective: User reviews results, downloads ZIP, and submits natural language corrections
- Implementation: Task detail page (status=`review`): result summary table showing jobs grouped by client, flagged items highlighted in yellow, warnings in orange. Download ZIP button. Correction panel: textarea + "Apply Correction" button → `POST /api/tasks/[id]/corrections` → saves to `CorrectionLog`, re-queues task. Re-upload panel: replace any input file → re-queues task. Status auto-refreshes every 3s via polling
- Demo: Processed task shows result table with flags; "remove job 3" correction re-triggers processing and updates output

**Task 10: Correction node in LangGraph**
- Objective: Apply natural language corrections to task state before re-generating output
- Implementation: `CorrectionNode` added to the graph — activated when `state.pendingCorrection` is set. Sends current result JSON + correction message to LLM → returns updated result JSON. Supported operations: remove job, add/remove/move part, edit quantity. After applying, graph continues to `GenerateOutputNode`. Unit tests with mocked LLM for each correction type
- Demo: "Move the toner cartridge from job 2 to job 4" → result JSON updated correctly → new ZIP generated

**Task 11: Task lifecycle completion & archive**
- Objective: User completes a task; completed tasks are archived and browsable
- Implementation: `POST /api/tasks/[id]/complete` sets status to `completed`. Home page: two sections — "Active Tasks" and "Completed Archive". Completed tasks show date, client count, download ZIP link. `DELETE /api/tasks/[id]` (admin only): removes DB record + deletes files from EBS. Completed tasks are read-only (no corrections)
- Demo: Complete a task → moves to archive; ZIP still downloadable; delete removes it from list and disk

---

Does this plan look good, or would you like me to adjust anything?

Good question to settle before we start building. Here's my thinking:

---

**UI Component Library**

For a data-heavy internal tool (tables, file uploads, status badges, modals) on desktop only, the realistic options are:

- **shadcn/ui** — not a library you install, it's copy-paste components built on Radix UI primitives + Tailwind. You own the code, no version lock-in, excellent TypeScript support, very popular in Next.js App Router projects. Best fit for a POC that might grow.
- **Ant Design** — full component library, has a powerful `Table` component with grouping/sorting built in (useful for your results view), but it's heavy, opinionated, and has its own CSS-in-JS that can conflict with Next.js SSR.
- **Mantine** — full library, good table/form components, works well with Next.js, lighter than Ant Design.

My recommendation: **shadcn/ui**. It gives you exactly what you need (Table, Dialog, Badge, Form, Tabs) without fighting the framework, and Tailwind handles all layout/spacing. For the results table with grouping you'd use **TanStack Table v8** underneath (shadcn's DataTable pattern already uses it).

---

**Styling**

**Tailwind CSS v4** — pairs naturally with shadcn/ui, desktop-only means no complex responsive breakpoint logic needed, utility classes keep styles co-located with components. No separate CSS files to maintain.

---

**State Management**

For this app, honestly: **probably not needed** as a separate library. Here's why:

- Task list, task detail, correction history → all server state fetched from your API
- **TanStack Query (React Query)** handles server state perfectly: caching, polling (for task status updates every 3s), invalidation after mutations. This replaces what you'd otherwise reach for Redux/Zustand for
- The only local UI state (open/close modal, which tab is active) is simple enough for `useState`

So: **TanStack Query for server state + `useState` for local UI state**. No Zustand/Redux needed for a POC of this scope.

---

**Summary proposal:**

| Concern | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Components | shadcn/ui + Radix UI | Owns the code, Next.js native, great DX |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4 | Co-located, desktop-only = simple |
| Data tables | TanStack Table v8 | Grouping, sorting, shadcn DataTable pattern |
| Server state | TanStack Query v5 | Polling, caching, mutations |
| Local UI state | `useState` | Nothing complex enough to warrant more |

Want me to lock this in and update the plan, or do you prefer a different direction on any of these?
lock this in the plan and let's discuss information interchang e protocol REST or GraphQL or GRPC. I prefer REST due simplicity but if you have another opinion, tell me.

REST is the right call here, and I agree with your instinct. Here's the quick reasoning:

**Why not GraphQL or gRPC:**
- GraphQL adds a schema layer, resolver boilerplate, and a client (Apollo/urql) — overkill when your data shapes are straightforward and you have maybe 10 endpoints
- gRPC is for service-to-service communication, not browser clients — wrong tool entirely here
- Both add complexity that works against the POC goal

**REST fits perfectly because:**
- Next.js App Router Route Handlers are REST-native
- TanStack Query works best with simple `fetch` calls to REST endpoints
- Your operations are resource-oriented: tasks, files, corrections, results — maps cleanly to REST nouns
- File uploads (multipart/form-data) are trivial with REST, awkward with GraphQL

**One nuance worth noting:** since you're using Next.js App Router, some of these "API calls" could be **Server Actions** instead of REST endpoints — particularly mutations like "mark complete" or "apply correction". Server Actions are essentially typed RPC calls co-located with your components, no fetch boilerplate needed. But for anything TanStack Query needs to poll or cache (task status, results), a proper REST route handler is cleaner.

**Proposed split:**
- REST route handlers (`/api/...`) — file uploads, task status polling, ZIP download
- Server Actions — simple mutations (complete task, delete task, save instructions)
